newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus satisfied with Greek election results.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus satisfied with Greek election results.

text.p: Cyprus expressed satisfaction on Monday at the outcome of parliamentary elections in Greece which gave Prime Minister Costas Simitis a fresh four-year mandate.
Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides, founder of the right-wing Democratic Rally party, said in a message to the leader of the socialist PASOK party he was happy to hear of his victory.
"It is with great joy that I was informed of your election victory....I wish you every success and look forward to the continuation of our close cooperation in all sectors," Clerides said.

Cyprus, divided since a 1974 Turkish occupation sparked by a brief coup engineered by the military regime then ruling Greece, is a frequent source of tension between Greece and Turkey, both NATO members. Greek and Turkish Cypriots continue to live apart with a U.N.-controlled buffer zone wedged between them.
Ankara has 30,000 Turkish troops in the northern third of the island, declared a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in 1983 which only Turkey recognises.
Demetris Christofias, leader of the Cypriot communist party Akel, the island's second largest party, called for better coordination between the two governments on the Cyprus dispute.

"I believe what Cyprus should ask for from Greece is a stronger presence at the U.N., in NATO and the European Union, bearing in mind that the policies of those who want to pamper Turkey are from there," said Christofias.
In the Turkish-held areas Taner Etkin, foreign and defence minister of the breakaway state, said the election results concerned the Greeks and the Greek Cypriots alone.

"Simitis and Evert have the same policy as the Greek Orthodox Church and the Greek Cypriots -- to Hellenise Cyprus. Both leaders are known for their anti-Turkish policies so it makes no difference for us who won in Greece," Taner told Reuters.

Mehmet Ali Talat, leader of the left-wing, main opposition Republican Turkish Party, said Simitis's victory will give him the chance to take "bold decisions" on Greco-Turkish relations and the Cyprus problem.

"He has the experience and the courage, with the strength of the support behind him to work for peace and better relations with Turkey. I believe Mr Simitis will be effective in establishing peace in Cyprus and peace and better relations with Turkey," he said.

Many Greek Cypriots living in the government-controlled south credit the PASOK leadership, and especially outgoing National Defence Minister Gerassimos Arsenis, for forging a defence pact with the island in November 1993.
Under terms of the pact, Greece will come to Cyprus's aid in the event of a Turkish attack on the island.
Simitis's popularity shot up during a fleeting eight-hour visit in August after two Greek Cypriots were killed during demonstrations in the buffer zone against Turkey's occupation.
In Cyprus, he reaffirmed his country's support to efforts for a peaceful solution to the problem, and to U.N. resolutions calling for the island to be reunited as a bicommunal federation.
